newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's ACOSS sees 97 welfare gap at 35 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: France's ACOSS sees 97 welfare gap at 35 bln Ffr.

text.p: France's social security accounts body ACOSS said on Tuesday it was sticking to its forecast of a 1997 welfare deficit of 35 billion francs.
An official said that after its latest review of accounts it had decided to maintain a forecast made earlier this year of a 2.7 percent rise in total wages.

It said it had revised down slightly its forecasts for pay rises, but this was offset by an improved outlook on job creations, meaning the forecast of a 2.7 percent rise in the total wage bill was unchanged.
ACOSS forecasts cash flow shortages in the social security system independently of the government.

French newspapers have suggested the social security deficit could reach 50 billion this year, threatening government efforts to cut the total public deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in preparation for European monetary union.
The government on Monday said there was no basis to this figure, though it acknowledged the deficit might be five billion francs more than the 30 billion forecast in the 1997 budget.

It said in a statement that the Social Security Accounts Commission, which also makes independent forecasts, had lowered its expectations for the rise in total wages to 2.7 percent, in line with ACOSS.

The 1997 budget forecast a rise in total wages of 3.3 percent. The difference in forecasts for wages growth would correspondend to a loss of receipts for the welfare system of five billion francs, the government statement said.
The social security system is funded mainly from payroll taxes and covers healthcare, pensions and family benefits.
